Also the "Typical Cases" like Case 1, etc. In Case 1: "Case 1: BOA BARGES etc... The case significance etc." At the end, "Case 1: ... created a great practice of protecting the rights etc" Not sure.

Option C: "The Nanjing Maritime Court promotes the quality of law enforcement and case handling through fair and efficient trial of cases; The Guangzhou Maritime Court illustrates its work results by listing its achievements."

Option D: "Nanjing Maritime Court adheres to the strategy of high-quality trials; The Guangzhou Maritime Court cited the results of high-quality cases."

Option A: "The Nanjing Maritime Court has won praise for improving the accuracy of case handling by formulating normative guidelines; The Guangzhou Maritime Court cited the results to explain."

That likely refers to "two departments" could refer to the process of building high-quality cases in the Nanjing Maritime Court (focus on careful procedural steps, guidelines, they formulate guidelines, refine trial process, etc.) and Guangzhou Maritime Court's mention of listing achievements and the results by listing data.

So Guangzhou had a list of "successfully recognized" cases. It also mentions that it presented results by listing "its achievements" such as "list of typical cases" with specific numbering and listing recognized cases. That points to "illustrates its work results by listing its achievements."

Thus, between options, Option C: Nanjing maritime court promotes quality through fair and efficient trial; Guangzhou illustrates its work results by listing achievements. This seems correct. That might be true: Guangzhou uses data like 'numbers of cases and percentages'. But "high-quality cases" is about producing quality. The Guangzhou court's "successful practice to deliver quality cases" uses "lists of recognized cases" which is basically "list achievements."

Option C: specifically quality of law enforcement and case handling through fair trial; Guangzhou illustrates results by listing achievements. That seems close.

Which better matches the phrasing: "What is the difference in the focus of the two departments in terms of creating high-quality cases?" The question could be referencing the difference: Nanjing emphasis on trial processes, Guangzhou emphasis on number and data. Option C is okay.

Option C says Nanjing promotes quality in law enforcement and case handling through fair and efficient trial; Guangzhou illustrates results by listing its achievements. The question "difference in the focus of the two departments in terms of creating high-quality cases?" The difference emphasises 'focus of the two departments'. Which one emphasises the process? Which one emphasizes results? Option C emphasises "promotes quality of law enforcement and case handling through fair and efficient trial" versus "illustrates results by listing achievements." Option B emphasises "trusted by international community for professional judicial ability." Both basically mention process vs data. Option C is more neutral.

Check again the source of Nanjing: "The Court carried out prospective research ... refining the trial process... etc." So Nanjing is focusing on fine-tuning trial process.
